verification_report.summary:
The entire submitted chapter was checked sequentially, including its definitions, every proof and the closing discussion. All new deductions pass under the explicitly accepted prerequisites. The ruled-surface illustration remains conditional on the supplied nef, nonzero-divisor and zero-square data; the separate envelope-recovery result is not independently certified here. The audit contains 18 statement records and five reference records.

The denominator is finite, positive and scales correctly. Distributional Stokes against dd^c-closed Gauduchon powers establishes nonnegativity, smooth gauge invariance and monotonicity for pseudoeffective differences without assuming closed backgrounds. A fixed test metric gives finiteness; the infimum of continuous linear functionals gives homogeneity, root concavity and upper semicontinuity.

On the positive cone, the accepted smooth Hermitian equation applies after choosing a positive representative. Matrix AM-GM gives the lower dual bound, and a conformal Gauduchon representative attains equality. Thus lambda_mu=c_theta(mu)^(1/n) and V_mu=c_theta(mu), with a unique minimizing ray for n>=2. In dimension one the denominator is 1 and all test metrics minimize. The big-implies-positive corollary follows from current monotonicity. Concavity equality is correctly reduced to a common minimizer and then a constant ratio of solution forms; the curve case uses the Green operator.

Smooth dependence with varying backgrounds follows from the implicit function theorem using a fixed mean normalization and the invertible augmented linearization (v,a)->tr_Omega(dd^c v)-a. Differentiating the top-form equation cancels the factors n. Multiplication by the conformal weight before integration gives exactly the displayed first-variation denominator, with no missing factor.

Nefness is independent of the auxiliary metric and implies pseudoeffectivity by normalized quasi-psh compactness. The nef-limit proof validly commutes two infima and identifies decreasing scalar limits; it asserts no limiting weak equation. Closed Stokes is used with the required hypotheses to obtain V_mu(theta)=integral theta^n for closed nef backgrounds on a Kahler manifold. Zero-value attainment forces a positive current to have zero trace, hence vanish; elliptic regularity then proves smooth dd^c-exactness. The converse and conditional nonattainment illustration are valid.

Measure comparison has the correct factors M^(-1/n) and m^(-1/n), proving measure-independent zero and positivity sets. On the positive cone, normalized smooth Monge-Ampere measures prove both directions of the mass-invariance criterion. The torus, Gauduchon-surface and Hopf consequences follow from the accepted examples. No converse to big-implies-positive, arbitrary-pseudoeffective mass criterion, birational law or b-divisor intersection identity is inferred.

After the required theorem-search query returned no matching result, web verification confirmed Collins' Theorem 2.13 and its context; the requested local source lines were also read. Its W=0 determinant-root specialization matches this setting, and its scalar corresponds to lambda_mu. The attribution is accurate, and the chapter's proofs were checked independently. [Collins, Theorem 2.13](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1903.10898).
